raw_response:
Such an invariant can exist only if the box/wobble- and edge-profile-conditioned null contains more than one orbit under the automorphisms of  $Q_6$  that preserve the 16 boxes and wobble geometry. If that conditioned set is a single orbit, every label-free graph functional is constant, and there is structurally nothing left to discover. Assuming multiple orbits remain, the strongest next target is not another edge count but the higher-order incidence geometry of those fixed edges.
Let  $\Pi=\{B_1,\ldots,B_{21}\}$  be the genetic-code partition. Let  $A_1,\ldots,A_{25}$  be the fixed within-box atoms obtained after the  $16\to25$  wobble-respecting split. Define the common null  $\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E}$  as all unlabeled regroupings of these 25 fixed atoms into 21 fibers such that:


The multiset of global fiber assembly signatures is unchanged, including the  $4+2$  and other multi-atom size patterns.


For every box/wobble-preserving edge orbit  $E_r$ , the multiset over fibers of cross-atom synonymous-edge counts

$$e_r(B)=\left|E_r\cap \binom{B}{2}\setminus\bigcup_{A_i\subset B}\binom{A_i}{2}\right|$$

is exactly the observed one.


Hence every within-box contribution, every wobble contribution,  $e_{\rm in}$ , its directional profile, and its distribution across fiber signatures are conditioned out.


Fiber names are ignored; two partitions differing only by a permutation of the 21 functional labels are one state.


Use uniform exact enumeration of  $\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E}$ . If that is too large, the acceptable substitute is a fixed-seed Metropolis chain based on a connected set of constraint-preserving switches, with uniform stationary distribution—not an arbitrary rejection shuffle. Markov-basis and color-preserving switch constructions are the relevant formal framework for such conditional sample spaces. arXiv+1
1. Cross-box 4-cycle partition-motif residual
This is the strongest first candidate. Edges are first-order objects in a cube; the next canonical objects are its square 2-faces.
Let  $\mathcal F_2^\times$  be the induced 4-cycles of  $Q_6$  not wholly contained in one fixed within-box atom. On each square  $F$ , forget the fiber names and retain only the cyclic equality pattern of its four vertices. Up to dihedral symmetry, the possible types are

$$4,\quad 3+1,\quad 2+2_{\rm adjacent},\quad 2+2_{\rm alternating},$$


$$2+1+1_{\rm adjacent},\quad 2+1+1_{\rm opposite},\quad 1+1+1+1.$$

Count these separately for every orbit  $o$  of cross-box square faces under the box/wobble-preserving automorphism group:

$$m_{o,\tau}(\Pi)
=
\#\{F\in o:\operatorname{type}(\Pi|_F)=\tau\}.$$

The resulting finite vector  $m_\square(\Pi)$  is label-free.
Some linear combinations of these counts are forced by the edge profile: each motif contains a known number of synonymous boundary edges, and each edge participates in a fixed number of square faces. Let  $A_\square m_\square$  be the complete vector of those fixed margins. Project onto their orthogonal complement:

$$z_\square
=
P_\square m_\square,\qquad
P_\square
=
I-A_\square^\top
(A_\square A_\square^\top)^+
A_\square.$$

This is the exact non-edge component of the square-motif census.
The omnibus extremality statistic is

$$T_\square
=
(z_\square-\mu_\Omega)^\top
\Sigma_\Omega^+
(z_\square-\mu_\Omega),$$

where  $\mu_\Omega$  and  $\Sigma_\Omega$  are the exact mean and covariance over  $\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E}$ . Its exact p-value is

$$p_\square
=
\frac{
\#\{\Pi'\in\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E}:
T_\square(\Pi')\ge T_\square(\Pi_{\rm std})\}
}{
|\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E}|
}.$$

The most interpretable coordinate is the count of diagonal recovery faces: squares having a same-fiber opposite pair but no synonymous boundary edge, corresponding to  $2+2_{\rm alternating}$  and  $2+1+1_{\rm opposite}$ . That measures synonymy expressed as a two-step diagonal recurrence rather than as edge hiding. It is not determined by  $e_{\rm in}$ , although the full omnibus statistic should be used to avoid selecting that coordinate after seeing the code.
This route fails if  $P_\square m_\square$  has zero variance on the conditioned null. In that case, the square structure is itself algebraically forced by the box/wobble and edge margins.
2. Residual boundary-channel topology of the fiber quotient
Edge hiding counts how many one-step changes remain inside a fiber. It does not specify how the unavoidable cross-fiber edges are distributed among pairs of fibers.
Construct the weighted, loopless quotient multigraph  $Q_\Pi$  on the 21 fibers:

$$W_{ab}
=
\#\{uv\in E(Q_6):u\in B_a,\ v\in B_b\},
\qquad a\neq b.$$

The total weight

$$\sum_{a<b}W_{ab}=|E|-e_{\rm in}$$

is fixed, so it is not the statistic. Strengthen the null for this route by also preserving, as an unlabeled multiset, every fiber’s boundary-degree vector by edge orbit:

$$d_r(B)=
\#\{uv\in E_r:u\in B,\ v\notin B\}.$$

Thus even the weighted degree sequence and directional boundary exposure of the quotient are conditioned out.
Let

$$L_W=\operatorname{diag}(W\mathbf 1)-W$$

be its weighted Laplacian. Define the exact weighted spanning-tree count

$$\tau(Q_\Pi)
=
\det L_W^{(i)},$$

where  $L_W^{(i)}$  is any principal cofactor. This is invariant under permutation of the fiber labels.
The functional interpretation is boundary-channel compression. With the same number of unavoidable nonsynonymous edges and the same boundary-degree sequence, a small  $\tau$  means those edges are arranged through comparatively few globally independent fiber-to-fiber channels; a large  $\tau$  means they form a highly redundant interface network.
The preregistered compression statistic is

$$T_{\rm chan}=-\log \tau(Q_\Pi),$$

with exact upper-tail test

$$p_{\rm chan}
=
\frac{
\#\{\Pi'\in\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E,d}:
T_{\rm chan}(\Pi')\ge T_{\rm chan}(\Pi_{\rm std})\}
}{
|\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E,d}|
}.$$

Here  $\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E,d}$  is the common null additionally fixing the boundary-degree vectors. A useful secondary statistic is

$$C_{\rm pair}=\sum_{a<b}W_{ab}^{\,2},$$

but it should not replace  $\tau$ :  $C_{\rm pair}$  measures interface concentration, whereas  $\tau$  also sees how those interfaces are connected globally.
This route is less promising than the square census because quotient statistics often collapse onto block-size and boundary-degree structure. It survives only if weighted quotient graphs with identical conditioned degrees still occupy multiple nonisomorphic topologies and the standard code is extreme among them.
3. External bypass conductance between disconnected components
This route directly examines what edge hiding does not measure: the ambient placement of disconnected pieces of the same fiber.
For each fiber  $B$ , let

$$G[B]=C_{B,1}\sqcup\cdots\sqcup C_{B,r_B}$$

be its connected components. Strengthen the null by preserving the unlabeled multiset of component sizes and induced component isomorphism types for every fiber signature. Thus component count, the Ser/Leu/Arg branch form, and all internal edges are already conditioned out.
For every pair  $C_{B,i},C_{B,j}$ , form the graph

$$G_{B,ij}
=
Q_6-\bigl(B\setminus(C_{B,i}\cup C_{B,j})\bigr),$$

contract  $C_{B,i}$  and  $C_{B,j}$  to terminals, and assign unit conductance to every remaining edge. Let

$$g_{B,ij}
=
\frac{1}{R_{\rm eff}(C_{B,i},C_{B,j};G_{B,ij})}$$

be their effective conductance through codons outside that fiber. Effective resistance is a standard graph invariant that integrates the multiplicity and lengths of all connecting paths, rather than only the shortest path. arXiv
Define

$$T_{\rm bypass}
=
\sum_{B:r_B>1}
\sum_{i<j}
g_{B,ij}.$$

Because the null fixes component sizes, shapes, and internal-edge profiles, variation in  $T_{\rm bypass}$  comes only from where the disconnected components are embedded relative to the rest of the cube.
The natural one-sided hypothesis is near-merge compensation: when a same-fiber edge cannot be hidden, the disconnected pieces are nevertheless placed so that many short external routes join them. Test

$$p_{\rm bypass}
=
\frac{
\#\{\Pi'\in\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E,\mathrm{comp}}:
T_{\rm bypass}(\Pi')\ge
T_{\rm bypass}(\Pi_{\rm std})\}
}{
|\Omega_{\mathrm{BW},E,\mathrm{comp}}|
}.$$

For an integer-valued audit, accompany conductance with the lexicographically sorted multiset

$$\left\{
\left(
d^{\rm ext}_{B,ij},
N^{\rm ext}_{B,ij}
\right)
\right\},$$

where  $d^{\rm ext}$  is the shortest externally routed distance and  $N^{\rm ext}$  is the number of such shortest paths. Conductance remains the primary statistic because it includes longer parallel routes as well.
The main danger is that this becomes a statistic tailored to the known disconnected Ser fiber. It is admissible only when defined and summed over all disconnected fibers without naming Ser or Stop, and when component structure itself is fixed in the null.
Structural verdict
The square-motif residual is the best next test. It is the first canonical invariant beyond edge counts, it is intrinsically defined on  $Q_6$ , and it asks whether synonymous edges are arranged unusually around coordinate 2-faces rather than merely being numerous. The bypass-conductance functional is the strongest global complement. The quotient spanning-tree statistic is worthwhile but has the greatest risk of again collapsing into composition.
Before interpreting any positive value, two algebraic checks are essential:


The statistic must have nonzero variance over the exact conditioned null.


The conditioned null must contain at least two box/wobble-preserving automorphism orbits.


If either fails, no label-free invariant of that type exists beyond the already fixed structure.
Sharpest next question: Is the standard code’s cross-box 4-cycle partition-motif residual extremal among all regroupings of the same 25 box/wobble atoms that preserve the complete per-fiber, per-edge-orbit synonymous-edge profile?
